answer: Cross-Epoch Fingerprint Anchoring. Each identity must publish a ferrous-weighted commitment to its own action history, chained across epochs so a clone cannot copy prior fingerprints without holding the original's private trajectory. A mismatch between the claimed fingerprint and behaviour observed at the jetty (real interaction points) freezes the identity for the next epoch. Attacker cost: every synthetic identity needs an independently maintained history chain, so forgery scales linearly in real upkeep, not in cheap copies. Divergence surfaces each pearl of inconsistency as a flag.
